scenes.tts: A yeast cell has no ruler. So how does it know when it is big enough to divide, and why would being too big hurt?
scenes.narration: A yeast cell has no ruler. So how does it know when it is big enough to divide, and why would being too big hurt?
scenes.caption: A yeast cell has no ruler. So how does it know when it is big enough to divide, and why would being too big hurt?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (colour map: RED = the brake Whi5, GREEN = the Start line and commitment, ORANGE = RNA and protein, the working contents, PURPLE = the genome, BLUE = the surface membrane, YELLOW = the gauge and questions). Left 60% of the frame: one budding-yeast cell drawn as a large translucent circle in cross-section, filling about 65% of the frame height, ORANGE fill at low opacity with evenly spaced small ORANGE dots drifting slowly, a thick BLUE rim, and a small PURPLE rounded block (the genome: drawn as a plain block with no nuclear envelope around it; the film never shows the nucleus) off-centre. Right 30%: an empty tall gauge outline, not yet labelled. As the first sentence plays the cell swells steadily; a small bud grows at its right edge, pinches off and drifts out of frame, and the mother starts growing again. On 'no ruler' a large YELLOW question mark rises beside the cell and stays; on 'too big' the cell swells past its usual size and its BLUE rim pulses twice.
Title 'Amount over Volume' fades in across the top for 2 s, TEXT colour, size 44, while the cell keeps swelling slowly underneath and the question mark fades out.

scenes.tts: One thing a cell can sense is a concentration: the amount of something, divided by the room it has. The gauge on the right reads it. Watch ten red dots. The number stays the same, the room grows, and the concentration falls.
scenes.narration: One thing a cell can sense is a concentration: the amount of something, divided by the room it has. The gauge on the right reads it. Watch ten red dots. The number stays the same, the room grows, and the concentration falls.
scenes.caption: One thing a cell can sense is a concentration: the amount of something, divided by the room it has. The gauge on the right reads it. Watch ten red dots. The number stays the same, the room grows, and the concentration falls.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE dots fade to near-invisible so the next point reads cleanly. Ten RED dots drift inside the cell; a counter under the cell reads '10 dots' and never changes. On 'The gauge on the right reads it' the gauge gets its label 'amount ÷ volume' (YELLOW, size 30) and fills from the bottom with a YELLOW bar. On 'the room grows' the cell's volume doubles smoothly (radius × 1.26) with a readout under it 'volume 1 → 2', the red dots spread apart, and the gauge bar falls in step, computed as 10 ÷ volume, from 10 to 5 (half height). Small corner tag 'computed'.

scenes.tts: A leading model, still debated, says budding yeast uses this as a ruler. Each newborn daughter, whatever its size, gets about the same dose of a brake protein called W H I five. It holds back Start, the point where the cell commits to dividing.
scenes.narration: A leading model, still debated, says budding yeast uses this as a ruler. Each newborn daughter, whatever its size, gets about the same dose of a brake protein called Whi5. It holds back Start, the point where the cell commits to dividing.
scenes.caption: A leading model, still debated, says budding yeast uses this as a ruler. Each newborn daughter, whatever its size, gets about the same dose of a brake protein called Whi5. It holds back Start, the point where the cell commits to dividing.
scenes.visual: The cell shrinks back to newborn size as if just released from its mother. The ten RED dots stay and a RED label 'Whi5: the brake' attaches to them. The gauge relabels 'Whi5 ÷ volume' and its bar rises back up with the smaller volume. On 'Start' a GREEN dashed horizontal line slides across the gauge at 40% of its height, labelled 'Start' in GREEN, size 30. Beside the cell a GREEN arrow labelled 'divide' appears with a RED padlock clamped on it. On 'leading model' a small YELLOW corner tag 'a leading model' (size 28) appears and stays until the end of s08.

scenes.tts: As the cell grows, the brake spreads through more room and the gauge sinks. At the green line the brake gives way, and the cell commits.
scenes.narration: As the cell grows, the brake spreads through more room and the gauge sinks. At the green line the brake gives way, and the cell commits.
scenes.caption: As the cell grows, the brake spreads through more room and the gauge sinks. At the green line the brake gives way, and the cell commits.
scenes.visual: Computed with invented numbers (corner tag 'computed, invented numbers'): a dose of 100 Whi5 molecules, still drawn as the ten RED dots, and a Start line at 2 per fL. The cell grows from 30 fL to 50 fL with a readout under it; the red dots drift apart; the gauge bar falls along 100 ÷ volume from 3.3 to 2.0 per fL and touches the GREEN line exactly as the readout reaches 50 fL. At the touch the line and the cell's rim flash GREEN, the RED padlock springs open, and a bud starts to grow at the cell's edge.

scenes.tts: Now two newborns, one small and one large, each with the same red dose. Which must grow more before it commits? Pause and decide.
scenes.narration: Now two newborns, one small and one large, each with the same red dose. Which must grow more before it commits? Pause and decide.
scenes.caption: Now two newborns, one small and one large, each with the same red dose. Which must grow more before it commits? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: The cell splits the frame into two newborn cells side by side, each with its own narrower gauge and its own GREEN Start line at the same height. Left cell small (readout '20 fL'), right cell twice the volume ('40 fL'). Each holds the same ten RED dots, so the left cell's dots are crowded; its gauge stands high (5 per fL) and the right one lower (2.5 per fL), both computed as 100 ÷ volume. A YELLOW question card fades in across the top: 'Which must grow more?'

Predict pause. Hold the two cells, their gauges and the YELLOW question card 'Which must grow more?'. Near-stillness by design: only the RED dots jitter gently inside each cell. No change in size or gauge level.

scenes.tts: The small one. Its dots start crowded, so its gauge starts higher, and it must grow more to dilute them. That works only because both got the same dose. In this simple model, both commit at the same size. Real cells are noisier, and close only part of the gap.
scenes.narration: The small one. Its dots start crowded, so its gauge starts higher, and it must grow more to dilute them. That works only because both got the same dose. In this simple model, both commit at the same size. Real cells are noisier, and close only part of the gap.
scenes.caption: The small one. Its dots start crowded, so its gauge starts higher, and it must grow more to dilute them. That works only because both got the same dose. In this simple model, both commit at the same size. Real cells are noisier, and close only part of the gap.
scenes.visual: The question card fades. Both cells grow at once at the same rate. The right cell goes from 40 to 50 fL and its gauge, falling along 100 ÷ volume, hits the GREEN line first and flashes GREEN; the left cell keeps growing from 20 to 50 fL and its gauge reaches the line later, then flashes GREEN. Tags slide in under them: '+30 fL' (left) and '+10 fL' (right); both readouts end at '50 fL'. On 'the same dose' a RED bracket joins the two dot counters with the label 'same dose at birth'. Corner tag 'computed, invented numbers'. On 'simple model' a YELLOW tag 'simple model' (size 28) sits over the two '50 fL' readouts; on 'noisier' the right-hand cell's GREEN line widens into a soft GREEN band (labelled 'real: a range', size 28) and the left cell's end readout blurs to a range below 50 fL, schematic.
Brief hold with motion: the two cells, now the same size, each start a bud, and the GREEN lines pulse once.

scenes.tts: That is the one idea: amount over volume. As a cell grows, it dilutes anything whose amount does not keep pace.
scenes.narration: That is the one idea: amount over volume. As a cell grows, it dilutes anything whose amount does not keep pace.
scenes.caption: That is the one idea: amount over volume. As a cell grows, it dilutes anything whose amount does not keep pace.
scenes.visual: The two cells merge back into one cell beside one gauge. The words 'amount ÷ volume' lift to the top centre in YELLOW, size 42; beneath them 'not keeping pace → diluted' types in, its arrow pointing at the RED gauge bar as the cell grows once more and the bar sinks again.

scenes.tts: For most other contents, dilution is a danger. R N A and protein, the orange dots, do the cell's work. So most growing cells make them roughly in step with their volume.
scenes.narration: For most other contents, dilution is a danger. RNA and protein, the orange dots, do the cell's work. So most growing cells make them roughly in step with their volume.
scenes.caption: For most other contents, dilution is a danger. RNA and protein, the orange dots, do the cell's work. So most growing cells make them roughly in step with their volume.
scenes.visual: The RED dots fade. The ORANGE dots return, evenly spaced, labelled 'RNA and protein' in ORANGE. The cell grows from 30 to 60 fL; new ORANGE dots pop in at random places as it grows, one for each bit of added volume, so the spacing never changes. A second gauge, ORANGE, labelled 'RNA and protein ÷ volume', appears beside the RED one; its bar stays level while the cell doubles. Corner tag 'computed'.

scenes.tts: Their gauge stays flat. Their total amount grows with the cell, but their concentration does not, so it cannot be the ruler.
scenes.narration: Their gauge stays flat. Their total amount grows with the cell, but their concentration does not, so it cannot be the ruler.
scenes.caption: Their gauge stays flat. Their total amount grows with the cell, but their concentration does not, so it cannot be the ruler.
scenes.visual: The two gauges tip over into a small chart under the cell, x axis 'cell volume' (no numbers), y axis 'amount ÷ volume'. A RED curve draws itself falling as 100 ÷ volume and crosses a GREEN dashed Start line; an ORANGE line draws itself flat. Labels slide in at their ends: 'ruler' on the red curve, 'flat: no size signal' on the orange line. On 'total amount' a small ORANGE counter under the cell ticks upward as new dots appear, while the ORANGE line stays flat. The cell keeps growing slowly above. Corner tag 'computed'.

scenes.tts: Two things can fall behind. First, the genome, the cell's D N A, drawn as the purple block. Yeast held so they grow without dividing kept one copy while they swelled many times over.
scenes.narration: Two things can fall behind. First, the genome, the cell's DNA, drawn as the purple block. Yeast held so they grow without dividing kept one copy while they swelled many times over.
scenes.caption: Two things can fall behind. First, the genome, the cell's DNA, drawn as the purple block. Yeast held so they grow without dividing kept one copy while they swelled many times over.
scenes.visual: The chart folds away; back to the single cell with its ORANGE gauge. The PURPLE genome block brightens and gets the label 'genome: one copy, held' in PURPLE. The GREEN divide arrow appears crossed out, labelled 'held: no division'. The cell balloons with a readout under it running 'about 65 → 600 fL' (the circle's radius grows about 2.1-fold, the cube root of the volume change); to fit, the camera pulls back smoothly. The PURPLE block stays exactly the same size throughout.

scenes.tts: Their synthesis fell behind, so their cytoplasm, the material outside the nucleus, was diluted: the orange dots thinned out. R N A is copied from the D N A. At such sizes, one genome copy appears to become a limit.
scenes.narration: Their synthesis fell behind, so their cytoplasm, the material outside the nucleus, was diluted: the orange dots thinned out. RNA is copied from the DNA. At such sizes, one genome copy appears to become a limit.
scenes.caption: Their synthesis fell behind, so their cytoplasm, the material outside the nucleus, was diluted: the orange dots thinned out. RNA is copied from the DNA. At such sizes, one genome copy appears to become a limit.
scenes.visual: As the cell keeps swelling, new ORANGE dots appear more and more slowly, so the gaps between them open up; the ORANGE gauge, level until now, sags. A tag on the gauge: 'schematic, no measured values'. On 'diluted' the word 'diluted' appears in ORANGE beside the gauge. On 'copied from the D N A' thin ORANGE strands flow out of the PURPLE block at a steady rate that does not rise as the cell swells. On 'a limit' the PURPLE block pulses once with a thin PURPLE ring, labelled 'a limit?'.
Brief hold with motion: the swollen cell drifts, its sparse ORANGE dots wander, and it slowly shrinks back to normal size as the camera returns, ready for the next scene.

scenes.tts: The second is the surface. Everything the cell takes in crosses its membrane, the blue rim. But it uses what it takes in throughout its volume.
scenes.narration: The second is the surface. Everything the cell takes in crosses its membrane, the blue rim. But it uses what it takes in throughout its volume.
scenes.caption: The second is the surface. Everything the cell takes in crosses its membrane, the blue rim. But it uses what it takes in throughout its volume.
scenes.visual: The cell at normal size. Its BLUE rim thickens and is labelled 'surface: supply' in BLUE. Twelve short BLUE arrows point inward across the rim and pulse in turn, like a ripple running round the cell. On 'throughout its volume' the ORANGE interior brightens and is labelled 'volume: demand' in ORANGE; its dots drift.

scenes.tts: Take a sphere, the simplest shape, and double its radius. The rim's area rises four times, the volume eight. So each bit of the inside has half as much membrane feeding it.
scenes.narration: Take a sphere, the simplest shape, and double its radius. The rim's area rises four times, the volume eight. So each bit of the inside has half as much membrane feeding it.
scenes.caption: Take a sphere, the simplest shape, and double its radius. The rim's area rises four times, the volume eight. So each bit of the inside has half as much membrane feeding it.
scenes.visual: The cell shrinks to sit on the left with a radius label '5 µm' and its twelve BLUE arrows; a copy grows out of it on the right to twice the radius, '10 µm'. Both cells are drawn as three-dimensional shaded spheres. As the big sphere grows, new BLUE arrows sprout across its whole surface at the same density as on the small one: it ends with 48 arrows, four times as many, over a surface four times as large. On 'the simplest shape' a small YELLOW tag 'sphere: simplest case' (size 28) appears. Under the pair, two bars grow: BLUE 'area × 4' and ORANGE 'volume × 8'. On 'half as much' the big cell is cut open to show faint three-dimensional volume sectors, one per arrow, each visibly twice the volume of a sector in the small cell, and a YELLOW readout appears: 'membrane per volume: ½' with 'area ÷ volume: 0.6 → 0.3 per µm' beneath it. Corner tag 'computed, sphere'. No supply or demand curves, and no crossing point.

Brief hold with motion: the arrows on both cells keep pulsing at the same density over the whole surface; the big cell's ORANGE interior breathes, its sectors (one per arrow, twice the volume of the small cell's) shimmer, and the 'membrane per volume: ½' readout stays.

scenes.tts: So one gauge does four jobs. A diluted brake may tell yeast its size. R N A and protein keep pace, so their concentrations stay steady. A single genome can fall behind, and so can a sphere's surface: two costs of being big.
scenes.narration: So one gauge does four jobs. A diluted brake may tell yeast its size. RNA and protein keep pace, so their concentrations stay steady. A single genome can fall behind, and so can a sphere's surface: two costs of being big.
scenes.caption: So one gauge does four jobs. A diluted brake may tell yeast its size. RNA and protein keep pace, so their concentrations stay steady. A single genome can fall behind, and so can a sphere's surface: two costs of being big.
scenes.visual: Four small gauges line up across the bottom, each moving once more in its own colour and with a two-word label: RED falling to a GREEN line ('a proposed ruler'), ORANGE flat ('kept steady'), ORANGE sagging beside a PURPLE block ('genome: a cost'), BLUE falling, labelled 'membrane per volume' ('surface: a cost'). Above them the single cell grows, buds and splits once.
End card: the line in TEXT colour, size 40, centred, over the faint four gauges.
scenes.line: Growth dilutes what does not keep pace: a proposed ruler, two costs.
